title: Flicker the Lost Dragon
markdown:
Whoooo-whoooo, gather ‘round, little dewdrop dwellers and sleepy buttercups. The ancient trees, with bark like kindly, wrinkled faces, remember this story from a time when the moon was only a whisper of silver in the night. It was in the Honeybell Highlands, where the air smells as sweet as a warm hug and makes you want to dream.

Otis Pine, a wizard with eyes as bright and curious as a little sparrow's, was out for a quiet walk. He was still learning his magic, so his wand sometimes went fizzle-pop! and sent out little clouds of sparkly dust that tickled his nose. He loved these quiet walks down the sleepy cedar trail. The only sounds were the soft rustle of leaves, like tiny secrets being shared, and the gentle sigh of the breeze as it tickled the branches. The stars, they twinkled like happy little fireflies sprinkled across the dark blue blanket of the sky.

Suddenly, a tiny, sniffly sound, like a tear falling on a flower petal, caught his ear. It was coming from behind some bluebells that shimmered in the moonlight. Otis, as light and quiet as a falling feather, tiptoed closer. And there, all curled up in a fuzzy, sad ball, was a little dragon. His scales were the warm colour of honey on a sunny day. His wings, which usually fluttered like beautiful autumn leaves, were drooping like tired flowers. He hiccuped a little puff of smoky grey air, and it smelled just like warm, freshly baked cookies!

"Oh, my goodness!" Otis whispered. His heart gave a little gentle hop. "Are you lost, little one?"

The dragon blinked his big, kind eyes. "Hic-hic," he sniffled. "I… I was chasing a firefly. It was so bright! And then… and then I couldn't find my sleepy cave." He hiccuped again, a bigger puff of smoke this time, which tickled Otis's nose like a playful little butterfly.

"Don't you worry your sweet little dragon head," Otis said, his voice as soft and warm as a fuzzy blanket. "I'm Otis Pine, and I know these woods like I know how to stir honey into tea. What's your name, little dragon?"

"Flicker," he whispered, his voice a tiny, rumbling sound, like a happy, faraway bumblebee. "Flicker the dragon."

"Flicker," Otis repeated, a warm smile spreading across his face like sunshine. "Well, Flicker, it's getting very close to dawn. We need to get you back to your sleepy cave before the sun starts peeking over the hills. Do you remember anything at all about where you live?"

Flicker thought very, very hard, his little dragon eyebrows creasing. "It smells… so warm," he said slowly. "And there are lots and lots of other dragons who like to snooze. And… and Mama always reads us sleepy stories before we drift off."

"That’s wonderful!" Otis exclaimed. His wand gave a happy, little fizz that sent out a shower of tiny, harmless sparks. "The dragon caves are usually tucked away where the mountains whisper secrets to the clouds. Let's follow this sleepy cedar trail. I think it leads towards the Whispering Peaks, where the mountains are very, very tall."

So, with Flicker trotting happily beside him, his little dragon feet making soft, pattering sounds on the mossy path, they began their journey. Flicker hiccuped occasionally, little puffs of smoke appearing like tiny, fleeting clouds in the dim light. Otis hummed a cheerful, quiet tune, and his wand sometimes sent out little sparks of light that danced around like friendly fireflies, just to keep Flicker’s spirits up.

As they rounded a bend, they saw a very, very tall figure sitting on a large, mossy rock. It was Barnaby Buttercup, the kindest ogre in all the Honeybell Highlands. His woolly beard, as soft as a baby lamb’s wool, reached almost to his knees, and his eyes were as warm and blue as a clear summer sky. He was gently coaxing a fluffy cloud-sheep, which looked like a ball of spun sugar, back into a cozy huddle.

"Hullo there, young Otis!" boomed Barnaby, his voice like a soft, friendly rumble of distant thunder. "And who is this little friend you have with you?"

"Hullo, Barnaby," Otis replied, beaming. "This is Flicker. He's trying to find his way back to his sleepy cave."

Barnaby peered down at Flicker, a wide, kind smile spreading across his face. "A dragon! Well, hello there, little Flicker! I saw some dragon folk heading towards the High Crags earlier this morning. They looked a little bit worried, muttering about a tiny one who was very fond of chasing fireflies."

Flicker’s little dragon ears perked up, like tiny radar dishes. "High Crags?" he whispered, his voice full of hope. "That sounds like my home!"

"Indeed it does," Barnaby nodded, his beard swaying gently. "Just follow this trail a little further, and you'll see the path that winds up, up, up towards the tallest peaks. The caves are hidden there, like secrets tucked away in the stone." He offered Flicker a big, gentle finger, which Flicker tentatively touched with his snout. "Be safe on your journey, little one."

Flicker, for the very first time that night, didn't hiccup. He gave a tiny, happy wiggle that made his honey-coloured scales gleam. "Thank you, Barnaby!" he chirped.

As they continued on their way, the sky began to lighten, like a painter adding soft colours to a canvas. The shy moon faded away, and a gentle, rosy glow appeared on the eastern horizon. Flicker shuffled a little closer to Otis, his tiny dragon paws stepping carefully. "Otis," he whispered, his voice a little wobbly, like wobbly jelly. "It's getting bright. What if… what if we can't find it?"

Otis stopped and knelt down, so he was eye-level with Flicker. He placed a gentle hand on Flicker’s warm, honey-coloured back. "Patience now, Flicker," he said softly, his voice like a comforting lullaby. "All will be revealed in time. And even if it takes a little longer, I am here with you. We are a team." He then showed Flicker his wand, which glowed with a gentle, reassuring light, like a warm ember. "And I have a little bit of magic to help, too."

Flicker leaned into Otis's comforting hand, feeling the warmth and the steady, kind presence. He hiccuped once, a tiny puff of smoke that smelled like sunshine and happy thoughts.

Soon, they reached a fork in the trail. One path wound downwards, promising a gentle descent, but the other, as Barnaby had said, wound upwards, towards the very tallest peaks that scraped the sky. "This is it!" Flicker chirped, a little burst of excitement bubbling inside him, like tiny champagne bubbles.

They climbed, the air growing cooler and smelling sweeter, like wild flowers. And then, just as the very first golden rays of the rising sun peeked over the distant mountains, they saw it. Tucked into a rocky cleft, a cave entrance, warm and inviting, with a faint, comforting scent of slumbering dragons and sleepy stories. And at the entrance, three sleepy dragon heads, their scales shimmering like the colours of the dawn, looked out with sleepy, hopeful eyes.

"Flicker!" a voice rumbled, soft and warm as a mother's hug.

"Mama!" Flicker squeaked, and with a happy, excited flap of his shimmering wings, he was off! He soared through the air, a streak of honey-coloured joy, and landed right in the waiting embrace of his family. He hiccuped, a joyous burst of smoky, happy giggles that filled the air with warmth and wonder.

Otis watched, his heart feeling as warm and full as a dragon’s hoard of sunshine. He saw Flicker snuggled between his parents, already looking very sleepy and ready for a good, long snooze in his familiar, cozy cave. Otis gave a little wave, a silent farewell.

As the sun climbed higher, painting the Honeybell Highlands in beautiful shades of gold and rose, Otis Pine walked back down the sleepy cedar trail. The woods were waking up, birds chirping their morning songs like tiny, happy bells, and the dew sparkled on every leaf like tiny diamonds. Otis felt a quiet joy bloom inside him, like a gentle flower. He hadn't performed any grand, dazzling spells, but he had helped a little dragon find his way back home. And that, he knew, was a truly wonderful kind of magic. Whoooo knows what other gentle adventures awaited him in the whispering woods? For now, his own cozy bed, and dreams filled with honey-coloured dragons, would be just perfect.
